survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This ICCS 2009 encyclopedia describes the study’s design and the qualitative national-context information collected alongside the ICCS 2009 survey. It reports that the student population was defined as Grade 8 students (or Grade 9 where the Grade 8 average age was below 13.5) and that data were collected in 38 countries from October 2008 to May 2009, with additional teacher and principal/contextual instruments. The excerpt does not specify whether complex survey weights (e.g., student sampling weights) or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were applied in any quantitative analysis, and it does not provide any weight variable names. For analysts using ICCS microdata, the appropriate approach is to apply the ICCS-provided complex survey weights and replicate weights when estimating population-representative statistics and standard errors; however, this encyclopedia volume itself is primarily descriptive/qualitative and does not document a weighting strategy for model-based inference.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The ICCS 2009 student population was defined as students in Grade 8 (approximately age 14) provided the average age in Grade 8 was at least 13.5 at the time of assessment; otherwise Grade 9 became the target population. In four countries (Greece, Norway, Slovenia, and Sweden), Grade 9 was also surveyed in addition to Grade 8 to enable comparability with the 1999 CIVED survey. The teacher population was defined as all teachers teaching regular school subjects to students in the target grade at each sampled school, restricted to teachers teaching the target grade during the testing period and employed at the school since the beginning of the school year. The encyclopedia volume itself reports qualitative national-context information and does not specify an analytic subsample beyond these study population definitions.

data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2009 investigated how countries prepare young people for civic roles by measuring students’ civic and citizenship knowledge, understanding, and reasoning, alongside student attitudes, perceptions, and activities related to civics and citizenship. The student cognitive test comprised 80 items across seven item-clusters administered via a balanced rotated design across seven booklets, with 45 minutes for the assigned booklet, and a 40-minute student questionnaire capturing background and perceptions. Data collection occurred in 38 countries between October 2008 and May 2009, with additional teacher questionnaires (30 minutes) and school/principal contextual instruments. The encyclopedia volume presents qualitatively oriented national-context chapters (for 35 of 38 countries) and uses these contexts to help interpret the quantitative ICCS 2009 survey results reported elsewhere. The excerpt does not provide any model-based performance metrics or PV/missing-data handling for empirical estimation within this volume.
